messages:
Maya: Heads-up — customer X (private VPC, EU-only egress) hit a P0 because our fallback routed them to us-west-2 when their control plane blocked that egress. Need a proposal for model-variant fallback that respects tenant egress allowlists and tiered routing.

Jordan: Oof. Did the control plane return a 403 or just ECONNREFUSED?

Maya: 403 from their firewall gateway. They have strict allowed_regions on control-plane -> inference egress. Our smart router assumed any region with compatible models was ok.

Eli: Short term: detect 403 on first request and stop trying that region for that tenant for X minutes. Longer term: incorporate tenant egress metadata into routing decisions.

Samir: Agreed on the 403 short-circuit. But question: where does the tenant metadata live? We currently store "allowed_regions" in Private customer profiles, but it's not surfaced in the routing API.

Anya: Right — console already shows allowed regions in Private -> Network, but the runtime routing service doesn't query it. We could add a small policy cache keyed by tenant_id.

Jordan: Adding the metadata to routing requires an API change: route(request) -> { tenant_id, model_hint, tier_hint } or we lookup tenant_id from request token. Which do we prefer?

Maya: Prefer lookup from token server-side to avoid clients having to know infra. But we must consider latency for the first request. Cache TTL should be e.g., 10m.

Eli: Cache approach fine. Also need to bake in model-variant compatibility. Example: tenant prefers redwood-13b-qa quantized in eu-west-1. If fallback model is redwood-13b-fp16 in eu-west-3, do we consider that compatible? We need compatibility rules.

Samir: We have a model-compat matrix in model-catalog svc. Could expose a lightweight boolean "compatible_with_variant" per pair. Router can prefer same-variant then cross-variant only if tenant allows broader variants.

Anya: UX question: console should show routing decisions and last N fallbacks per tenant. Ops asked for this for debugging. Telemetry footprint needs to be low for high-volume customers. Maybe sample fallbacks and show counts + last example.

Maya: Good point. Also quota implications: if we fallback to cheaper variant in-region to satisfy egress rules, billing and SLA differ. Need to surface to customer (and our billing pipeline).

Jordan: Policy idea (pseudocode):
```
policy: {
  allowed_regions: [eu-west-1, eu-west-3],
  tier: "dedicated",
  preferred_variants: [quantized-4bit, fp16],
  fallback_order: [in-region-same-variant, in-region-other-variant, cross-region-same-variant] // but omit cross-region if not allowed
}
```

Eli: Router algorithm: 1) read tenant policy from policy-cache, 2) filter candidate endpoints by allowed_regions, 3) score by variant match + latency + cost delta, 4) try best endpoint with fast failover. If endpoint returns control-plane-block (403/451) mark region as blocked for tenant for 30m and auto-replan.

Samir: Telemetry: emit an event on fallback with fields: tenant_id, source_region, attempted_region, model_variant_from, model_variant_to, reason. Use sampling 1% for high-traffic tenants, 100% for alerts.

Anya: Console: per-tenant "Routing" tab showing current policy, recent fallbacks (sampled), and a preview of what would happen if we change allowed_regions. Also a toggle for "strict egress enforcement" that prevents any cross-region fallback even if compatible.

Maya: API debate: should we expose a "routing_hint" in the public API so customers can opt-in to prefer same-region behavior? Pros: gives app control. Cons: complicates public surface and can be spoofed.

Jordan: If it's opt-in, fine. Default must be server-enforced using tenant policy. Private customers should never be forced cross-region by default.

Eli: Edge case: what if in-region endpoints are overloaded and cross-region is the only way to maintain latency SLOs? For certain enterprise tiers we might allow an "emergency cross-region" policy with explicit customer consent and audit logs.

Samir: We need a migration plan: 1) deploy policy-cache read-only, 2) update router to respect allowed_regions with a feature flag, 3) add 403 short-circuit, 4) roll flag on for Private tenants only, 5) console telemetry + UI.

Anya: UX mock note: expose a per-tenant toggle "allow_cross_region_fallback" + an audit log link.

ops-bot: deploy bot: canary of policy-cache service deployment succeeded in us-east-1 at 2025-03-12T15:12:03Z :white_check_mark:

Maya: Action items: Jordan + Eli own router change + short-circuit (PR by EOD Tues). Samir + Anya own telemetry + console mock (sync Wed). I'll draft an RFC with policy shape and compatibility matrix.

Jordan: quick Q — TTL for region block? 30m conservative; maybe make it adaptive (exponential backoff) to avoid flapping.

Eli: adaptive backoff makes sense. Start with 5m then double up to 2h.

Maya: Cool. I'll add that to RFC. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
